When getting agent pairs, complex results show up in
all their permutations. Make it so they only show up
once, and preferably such that they will almost always
show up with the agents that were queried (because
there will in general be more examples of such).

This is done by not returning agent JSONs for which
all represented hashes are complexes that have already
been represented. This means the limits and offsets no
longer directly map to those sent to the database,
which was long maintained for simplicity. However,
the machinery already existed to supply a custom offset
for the next page in the response, which is now once
again utilized in this case.

To allow for continued filtering across paging, the
complex hashes that were already displayed are sent as
part of the response, and it is recommended that paging
queries return this set in the next query as part of
the class initialization.

all their permutations. Make it so they only show up

there will in general be more examples of such).

This is done by not returning agent JSONs for which
all represented hashes are complexes that have already
been represented. This means the limits and offsets no
longer directly map to those sent to the database,
which was long maintained for simplicity. However,
the machinery already existed to supply a custom offset
for the next page in the response, which is now once
again utilized in this case.

To allow for continued filtering across paging, the
complex hashes that were already displayed are sent as
part of the response, and it is recommended that paging
queries return this set in the next query as part of
the class initialization.

When using a path with a tilde `~` on unix-like systems, the path is
interpreted as a literal `./~`, meaning a directory named `~` in the
current working directory. Users typically do not want this and would
probably be surprised by this behavior. I know I was surprised when I
ran histoqc and then saw a new directory named `~`. I removed it very
carefully, trying to be sure I didn't trash my home directory :)

This commit fixes the issue by expanding the tilde into the path to the
home directory. If a path does not begin with a tilde, the path is
unchanged.

use multi-stage build in Dockerfile to halve size

This commit proposes using a multi-stage Dockerfile. In the first stage,
we use the official python:3.8 image, which includes a C compilers. We
install the project and its dependencies. We create a dedicated virtual
environment for the project. Then in the second stage, we copy over the
project files and the python virtual environment, and we install
libopenslide0, which is required for openslide-python runtime.

This results in a more complex Dockerfile, but the resulting image is
half as big as the original (671 MB from about 1.3GB). I am also happy
to maintain this Dockerfile and answer any questions about it.

let fpgrowth and fpmax work directly with sparse input (#622)

* let fpgrowth and fpmax work directly with sparse input

If transactions are stored in a sparse matrix, it was first converted
into a dense Numpy array in setup_fptree before processing.

This commit allows to build the FPTree directly from sparse input, which
may save memory and processing time.  This is used by both fpgrowth and
fpmax.  There is no change after FPTree is being built.

* in setup_fptree, ensure that sparse DataFrame has no zeroes

In a212806 we assumed that all values in sparse DataFrame are non null,
which should always be true.  In order to avoid this corner case, we
now call itemsets.eliminate_zeros().  The alternative would be to replace
   nonnull = itemsets.indices[itemsets.indptr[i]:itemsets.indptr[i+1]]
by
   values = itemsets.data[itemsets.indptr[i]:itemsets.indptr[i+1]]
   nonnull = itemsets.indices[itemsets.indptr[i] + values.nonzero()[0]]
but it is slower.

Let apriori always use low_memory processing

Thanks to previous optimizations, processing with low_memory=True is
now as efficient as with low_memory=False, and allows to process much
larger datasets.

Removing processing with low_memory=False makes code simpler.

The downside is that we do not know in advance the number of itemsets to
process, thus it is displayed afterwards.  We now display the number of
itemsets after prune step.
Note that commit 2f928cb introduced a bug, the number of processing
combinations was multiplied by itemset's length.

Since vectorized operations are no more performed on frequent itemsets,
they are stored as list of tuples.

Apriori: implement join step of apriori-gen

The apriori-gen function described in section 2.1.1 of Apriori paper
has two steps; first, the join step looks for itemsets with the same
prefix, and creates new candidates by appending all pairs combinations
to this prefix. Here is pseudocode copied from paper:

  select p.1, p.2, ..., p.k-1, q.k-1
  from p in L(k-1), q in L(k-1)
  where p.1 = q.1, ..., p.k-2 = q.k-2, p.k-1 < q.k-1

The reason is that if a sequence q with the same prefix as p does not
belong to L(k-1), itemset p+(q.k-1,) cannot be frequent.
Before this commit, we were considering p+(q.k-1,) for any q.k-1 > p.k-1.

The second step of apriori-gen function is called prune step, it will
be implemented in a distinct commit.

See discussion in #644.

Ticket #547: Minor change: timeoutHint verification is not required to use request timestamp

We used the request timestamp to check the elapsed time since request was sent in order to evaluate the timeoutHint of publihs requets.
Since it is not required by the OPCUA spec part 4, we should not use the request timestamp and only use the current local time as reference for timeout.
It avoids clock synchronization issue between client and server.

OPC UA spec part 4:
- request timestamp definition:
  "The time the Client sent the request. The parameter is only used for diagnostic and logging purposes in the server."
  => i.e.: the server shall not use it for a functional behavior (e.g.: compute publish request timeout ...)
- request timeoutHint definition:
  "For a Server this timeout is only a hint and can be used to cancel long running operations to free resources."
  "The Server shall check the timeoutHint parameter of a Publish request before processing a Publish response."

Ticket #623: server SC key renewal bugfix: in key renewal transitory case, server uses old tokenId with new key sets

On server side, after sending the OPN renew response. The new security key set and associated tokenId is available as current key set but is not yet activated.
Its activation occurs only after the first client request with the new tokenId (and use of new security key sets associated). Therefore if the server shall send a response before the activation of the new key sets it shall use the old tokenId and security key sets associated.

Before this fix the server was using the old tokenId as expected but the new security key sets were used instead of previous one.
It leads the message signature to be invalid in sign mode and the messsage encryption and signature to be invalid in sign&encrypt mode.

translate_browse_path_result for the op compute_browse_result.

translate_browse_path_result.

into account of isBrowseResultAllocated.

For mingw docker:
When adding mbedtls/check libraries installed in the standard libraries of mingw, some headers of mingw seem to be included as well.
E.g.: mbedtls headers mbedtls/*.h are installed in /usr/i686-w64-mingw32/include/ which is considered the mbedtls include path since we use "#include mbdetls/<header.h>". When building code dependant on mbedtls this path is included and leads to include mingw headers that are not supposed to be.
It has (at least) for consequence to make fail tests sopc_ieee_check.h verication on float representation.
The current fix consists to install the mbedtls/check libraries in separate paths from mingw standard libraries to avoid including the mingw standard libraries directory to compile.

Ticket #447: Clear SOPC_AddressSpaceItem values in SOPC_AddressSpace_Delete

When using an embedded address space, the items should not be freed,
since they where not malloced. Their values however can have been
modified at runtime, and need to be freed in any case.

We address this by setting the "DoNotClear" flag on item values embedded
in the binary, this flag gets reset when the value is changed at
runtime. By setting the SOPC_Dict from the address space to clear all
values in its free function, we ensure that all malloc'ed values are
cleared when the address space is freed.

Ticket #1152: Update typing of 'next' in iterators

Specification of some iterators use 'next' and increase it for each
loop. Variables 'next' being bound (NAT1), a non overflow PO must be
proven at the exit of the last iteration of the loop (<= MAXINT).
This PO is unprovable.

As the 'next' variables are abstract, they can be typed by unbounded
integer set NATURAL1. As 'next' is assigned to an output parameter of
operations 'continue_iter_', the output parameter must be typed with an
implementable type (NAT1) in a before-after predicate.

This commit also removes redundant precond 'nb_browsePathSourceIdx_max_refs > 0'
from the operation 'continue_iter_browsePathSourceIdx'

Ticket #1274: SC layer: ensure internal send message is not interupted by extern event

Since sending an OPC UA message is done in 2 times: 1 external event received, 1 internal event triggered and then 1 internal event received.
It is possible that a SC_SERVICE_SND_MSG event is treated but another external event close the secure channel before the associated INT_SC_SND_MSG_CHUNKS internal event generated is treated.
But on an external point of view we want to be able to rely on the external event enqueued to ensure a message is sent prior to SC is closed (ApplyChanges method call request expecteds response to be sent).

As a consequence, use the SOPC_SecureChannels_EnqueueInternalEventAsNext to ensure internal event is treated in priority for sending messages.
Note: it cannot preempt an internal close event channel since it is emitted by the same thread

Ticket #1363: Correct op treat_browse_result_one_source_1

In the current implementation of treat_browse_result_one_source_1, the
browse result node Id is added to BrowsePathResult if its browse name
matches the target name. This leads to unprovable PO of preservetion of
imported machine invariant ran(BrowsePathResult) <: dom(conv_ExpandedNodeId_NodeId).

As the current B model does not deal with the case when the browse name
is out of date (cf. Table 167 of OPC UA Part 4 : local Server might not
continuously monitor the remote Server for changes), the above check of the
target name against the browse name is sufficient in the point of view
of protocol implementation. However, the operation shall be corrected in
order to :
 - Cover the specification of OPC UA even if the out of date of browse
   name has not been implemented yet,
 - Make the above PO provable.

The correction includes :
 - first of all, check if the server is local (expanded node Id can be converted
 into node Id),
 - then check if the browse name matches the looking target name.

Ticket #1363: Fix memory leak in compute_browse_result

In the implementation of operation compute_browse_result,
fill_browse_result is called if memory allocation is OK.
- In the case where fill_browse_result returns e_sc_ok, browse results
  are computed (compute_browse_result returns either e_sc_ok or
  e_sc_bad_no_continuation_points).
- In the cases where fill_browse_result does not return e_sc_ok, browse
  results are considered not computed. However, the memory stays allocated
  and will not be freed. Indeed, browse result memory freeing is performed by
  clear_browse_result or getall_and_move_browse_result. These operations
  are called only if compute_browse_result returns e_sc_ok or
  e_sc_bad_no_continuation_points.

Therefore, allocated memory shall be freed if compute_browse_result does
not return e_sc_ok or e_sc_bad_no_continuation_points.

Ticket #956: Client reverse connection fix: server socket shall be associated to SC token

Associate a waiting SC with a server socket connection was not a good idea, socket index was overwritten in case of several server connections.
And since we do not know on server connection if the server is the expected one we should not restrict the number of server connections to the number of waiting connections either.
We have to wait the RHE to know if the server is an expected one or not.
Therefore the concept of secure connection token is added to associate temporarely an SC token and a socket. An associated timeout is created to close the connection if no RHE is received.
Once the RHE is received, if no connection is compatible the SC token is cleared and socket is closed. Otherwise the content of the waiting SC is copied in the SC token to keep the
SC <-> socket association and the waiting SC index is released

The postcond of fill_browse_result_ref gives details of how updating
output variables. These details are not necessary. In fact, invariant of
imported machine browse_treatment_result_bs and invariant of while loop
in the calling operation fill_browse_result have no need of such
details. Furthermore, these details generate many POs to verify operation
refinement, invariant of imported machine and invariant of while loop in
the calling operation. Many of these POs can not be proved automatically.
The postcond of fill_browse_result_ref should be simplified by
specifying only necessary predicates. In this commit, variable typing is
introduced. Other predicates can be added by further examination of
generated PO.

Ticket #307: Bugfix Socket layer: assertion fails on socket connection failure

The problem was not visible before Ticket #330.
On socket connection failure, the socket network manager was generating a FAILURE event for socket event manager but state of the socket was not changed.
It seems that if the socket is used again for new network events before being closed, a socket write network event was triggered and leading to interpret it as a connection success (immediate state changed by network manager).

The bugfix consists to add a new intermediary state of CONNECTING_FAILURE set by the socket network manager in this case to avoid to check new network events on this socket before the socket event manager treats the failure and definitively close the socket.

Ticket #1152: Rewrite impl of treat_one_translate_browse_path

The op treat_one_translate_browse_path calls
treat_one_translate_browse_path_1 which implements a WHILE loop.
However, the init_iter_X op is called in treat_one_translate_browse_path
and the continue_iter_X is called in treat_one_translate_browse_path_1.
This makes it difficult to establish loop invariant. Furthermore, the
init_iter_X operation, which defines the entry of the loop, should
not be used to check other conditions not related to the loop. The check
of relative path size can be done by using the operation
read_RelativePath_Nb_RelativePathElt.

Therefore, init_iter_X is grouped with continue_iter_X in the operation
treat_one_translate_browse_path_1.

In addition, a new operation (update_one_browse_path_source) is created to
encapsulate the check and addition of a new node into BrowsePathSource.

Ticket #623: server SC key renewal bugfix: in key renewal transitory case, server uses old tokenId with new key sets

On server side, after sending the OPN renew response. The new security key set and associated tokenId is available as current key set but is not yet activated.
Its activation occurs only after the first client request with the new tokenId (and use of new security key sets associated). Therefore if the server shall send a response before the activation of the new key sets it shall use the old tokenId and security key sets associated.

Before this fix the server was using the old tokenId as expected but the new security key sets were used instead of previous one.
It leads the message signature to be invalid in sign mode and the messsage encryption and signature to be invalid in sign&encrypt mode.

message. The only constraint on requestedMaxReferencesPerNode is its
type UInt32. The implementation in C of get_browse_request_params
(msg_browse_bs) confirms this statement.

This limitation is treated in the operation compute_browse_result by
calling min_nb_result_refs.

Therefore, the above invariant must be deleted.

Ticket #1152: Rewrite translate_browse_path architecture

The translate_browse_path_i component should be rewritten as its size is
too big. One solution is to re-organize operations implementing
breadth-first-search of browse path when computing browse results.
The search uses variables BrowsePathSource, BrowsePathResult and
BrowsePathRemaining, which are initially encapsulted in the component
translate_browse_path_1. The re-organization is done as follows :
- Create the translate_browse_path_result module encapsulating operations
related to access / update of BrowsePathResult and BrowsePathRemaining.
- Create the translate_browse_path_source module encapsulating operations
related to access of BrowsePathSource and some basic operations related
to update of this variable. Not all update BrowsePathSource operations
can be integrated in this module : in fact, the update of BrowsePathSource
depends on BrowsePathResult and vice-versa. The SEES link is not
symmetric. The choice in this re-organisation is that
translate_browse_path_result SEES translate_browse_path_source.

This re-organisation results in modifications:
- Operations in translate_browse_path_1 are dispatched to
translate_browse_path_source_1 and translate_browse_path_result_1.
- Some local operations in translate_browse_path_i are dispatched to
translate_browse_path_source and translate_browse_path_result. The
component translate_browse_path_i keeps the sequencing of process of
BrowsePathSource and BrowsePathResult and some update operations for
BrowsePathSource.

Ticket #547: Minor change: timeoutHint verification is not required to use request timestamp

We used the request timestamp to check the elapsed time since request was sent in order to evaluate the timeoutHint of publihs requets.
Since it is not required by the OPCUA spec part 4, we should not use the request timestamp and only use the current local time as reference for timeout.
It avoids clock synchronization issue between client and server.

OPC UA spec part 4:
- request timestamp definition:
  "The time the Client sent the request. The parameter is only used for diagnostic and logging purposes in the server."
  => i.e.: the server shall not use it for a functional behavior (e.g.: compute publish request timeout ...)
- request timeoutHint definition:
  "For a Server this timeout is only a hint and can be used to cancel long running operations to free resources."
  "The Server shall check the timeoutHint parameter of a Publish request before processing a Publish response."

Ticket #1363: Fix memory leak in treat_one_relative_path_element_2

In the op treat_one_relative_path_element_2, clear_browse_result is
called only if compute_browse_result_from_source returns e_sc_ok.
However, compute_browse_result_from_source can allocate memory for
browse results even if the return code is not e_sc_ok. It is the case
where the return code is e_sc_bad_query_too_complex. This code can be
obtained when compute_browse_result, called by
compute_browse_result_from_source
returns e_sc_bad_no_continuation_points.

Ticket #447: Clear SOPC_AddressSpaceItem values in SOPC_AddressSpace_Delete

When using an embedded address space, the items should not be freed,
since they where not malloced. Their values however can have been
modified at runtime, and need to be freed in any case.

We address this by setting the "DoNotClear" flag on item values embedded
in the binary, this flag gets reset when the value is changed at
runtime. By setting the SOPC_Dict from the address space to clear all
values in its free function, we ensure that all malloc'ed values are
cleared when the address space is freed.

Ticket #307: Bugfix Socket layer: assertion fails on socket connection failure

On socket connection failure, the socket network manager was generating a FAILURE event for socket event manager but state of the socket was not changed.
It seems that if the socket is used again for new network events before being closed, a socket write network event was triggered and leading to interpret it as a connection success (immediate state changed by network manager).
